extracted.intended_audience: aspiring first-time novelists / writers starting their first novel
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, high-level stepwise guidance for planning, drafting, and revising a first novel, focused on story, character, structure, and establishing productive writing habits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand What You're Writing and Why
rubrics_metrics.description: Define success criteria; identify target readers; research 5–10 comparables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide what 'success' means for this book (e.g., publishing route, target sales, readership, personal goals). Identify your target readers so you can write to their expectations, and research 5–10 comparable titles to understand market, tone, and positioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fill Your Creative Well
rubrics_metrics.description: Document 'sparks' — ideas, quotes, sensations — in notebooks or apps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep a system (notebook, notes app) to capture inspirations and 'sparks' that can feed scenes, characters, and sensory detail. Regularly gather input to replenish ideas before and during drafting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write a Story, Not Just Words
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn Three Act Structure; avoid delivering 'a load of typing, instead of a story.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on story shape and causal narrative rather than isolated scenes or prose. Study Three Act Structure (or equivalent story-architecture models) to ensure scenes build stakes, conflict, and progression rather than meandering text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a Compelling Protagonist
rubrics_metrics.description: One main character; ask: What does she want? What stops her? How does she overcome? How is she changed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Center the novel on a single compelling protagonist with clear desires, obstacles, agency, and an arc of change. Use the listed questions as a minimum character-development checklist to ensure motivation and transformation drive the plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop Plot and Setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use plot and setting deliberately; use setting to create conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design plot beats and use setting not just as backdrop but as a functional source of obstacles, tone, and thematic resonance. Ensure scenes exploit setting to raise stakes or complicate the protagonist's goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Get Words on the Page
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule writing time; use short focused blocks (e.g., ten minutes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish regular writing habits with scheduled sessions and sprint-style focused blocks to overcome inertia. Accept that early drafting prioritizes momentum over polish — remember 'The first draft of anything is shit.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Embrace Rewriting
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-edit by printing; invest in professional editors. 'Writing is rewriting.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan substantial revision phases: print and edit on paper for distance, perform multiple passes (structure, character, line-level), and budget for professional editing (developmental, copyediting, proofreading). Treat rewriting as the central part of producing a publishable novel.
